mil4.6:1.1: The elder said “Good!” and, accepting it, explained the ten qualities of a lay follower.
mil4.6:1.2: “These, Great King, are the ten qualities of a lay follower.
mil4.6:1.3: Which are the ten: here, Great King, a lay follower shares in the joys and sorrows of the Saṅgha, is a master of the Dhamma, takes his share of the alms given as his strength allows, and on seeing the decline of the dispensation of the Buddhas grows zealous and strives.
mil4.6:1.4: He is of right view, has laid aside idle curiosity and grumbling, looks to no other teacher even for the sake of his life, guards his body and speech, has a harmonious resort and takes pleasure in harmony, is attentive, and does not walk in the Dhamma by the crooked path of deceit. He has gone for refuge in the Buddha, has gone for refuge in the Dhamma, has gone for refuge in the Saṅgha.
mil4.6:1.5: These, Great King, are the ten qualities of a lay follower; all of those qualities are present in three ways. It is fitting, appropriate, and suitable for you, on seeing the decline of the dispensation of the Buddhas, to wish to increase your zeal. I give you the opportunity; ask me as you please.”
mil4.6:2.1: The Question of Mendaka is finished.
